title: NexusMind
description: Multi-tenant memory control plane for AI engineering teams, with an MCP server as the front door
longDescription: A Rust + Axum control plane that gives AI coding tools (Claude Code, Cursor, any MCP client) a shared, auditable team memory. Every developer gets a scoped API key; every store, search and delete is written to an audit trail. Ships with a TypeScript MCP server, a React admin panel, and single-command Docker Compose deployment.

data.label: MCP Clients
data.description: Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot — any MCP-compatible tool
data.details: Agents talk to NexusMind through the Model Context Protocol over stdio. The client never sees the database or the API key of another tenant — it only knows the tools exposed by the MCP server.

data.label: Admin Panel
data.description: Browse memories, manage users, inspect the audit log
data.details: React 19 + Vite 5 + Tailwind v4 SPA using TanStack Query v5 for server-state. Read-heavy: memory browser, user management, per-org settings and audit inspection without touching SQL.

data.label: MCP Server
data.description: Translates MCP tool calls into REST calls
data.details: TypeScript server built on @modelcontextprotocol/sdk. Exposes store_memory, search_memories, get_context, record_decision and the SDD/task tools. Stateless — it forwards the developer's API key to the backend and returns typed results.

data.label: Auth Middleware
data.description: API key per user, scoped to an organization
data.details: Axum middleware layer. Cookie-first extraction with a `Authorization: Bearer nm_…` fallback. Resolves the key to a (user, org) pair and injects the tenant scope into every downstream query, so cross-tenant reads are impossible by construction rather than by convention.

data.label: REST API
data.description: Rust + Axum core — memories, context, SDD, tasks, policy
data.details: Modular router split by domain: memory, context, search, conventions, tasks, sdd, harnesses, policy, usage, admin. Each module owns its routes and handlers, which keeps the surface auditable as it grows past 200 endpoints.

data.label: Embedding Indexer
data.description: Semantic search over team memories and code
data.details: Background indexer that embeds memory content and repository symbols so search_memories and locate_code can rank by meaning instead of keywords. Ranked matches are filtered by tenant before they leave the process.

data.label: SQLite
data.description: Single-file store, bundled — no external database to operate
data.details: rusqlite with the bundled SQLite build, so the whole deployment is one binary plus one file. Schema migrations run at boot. Chosen deliberately over Postgres: the workload is read-heavy, per-tenant and small enough that operational simplicity beats horizontal scale.

data.label: Audit Trail
data.description: Every store, search and delete is logged
data.details: Append-only record of who did what, from which tool, and when. This is the feature that makes shared AI memory acceptable to a team: an admin can always answer 'where did this convention come from?'.

data.label: GitHub Actions
data.description: Builds, tests and publishes the backend image
data.details: ci.yml runs backend build, tests and clippy, the admin build and an MCP smoke test on every push. deploy.yml builds the arm64 backend image and pushes it to GHCR.

data.label: GHCR
data.description: Container registry for the backend image
data.details: Publishes ghcr.io/<owner>/nexusmind-backend:main-arm64. The host pulls by tag, so a deploy is a pull plus a container restart rather than a build on the box.

data.label: Cloudflare DNS
data.description: DNS plus the ACME DNS-01 challenge
data.details: Caddy solves ACME over DNS-01 instead of HTTP-01, using a token scoped to Zone:DNS:Edit. That lets a valid certificate be issued for the API hostname while the A record still points at the old host — which is what makes the cutover zero-downtime: bring the new box fully up, validate it, then move DNS.

data.label: Caddy
data.details: caddy-cloudflare 2.11.4. Terminates TLS for the public API hostname, compresses with zstd and gzip, and reverse-proxies to the backend container on port 8080.

data.label: Backend container
data.description: The Rust API, pulled by tag from GHCR
data.details: Runs the Axum server on 8080. Not exposed to the internet directly — only Caddy reaches it, over the compose network.

data.label: nexusmind_data
data.description: Named volume holding the SQLite file
data.details: State lives in a named Docker volume, so the container is disposable: replacing it on deploy does not touch the database.

data.label: Firebase Hosting
data.description: Admin panel and landing, served as static sites
data.details: Two hosting sites provisioned by Terraform. The SPAs are static and call the API across the public hostname, so the frontend deploy is fully decoupled from the backend one.

data.label: Terraform
data.details: Declares the Compute Engine instance, a persistent disk, a reserved static IP, HTTP and SSH firewall rules, an Artifact Registry repository and a service account scoped to read from it, plus both Firebase Hosting sites. Workload Identity Federation is scripted so CI authenticates without a long-lived key.

endpoints.description: Persist a decision, convention or discovery. Scoped to the org behind the API key.

endpoints.name: Search Memories
endpoints.description: Semantic search across the team's memories, ranked by embedding similarity.

endpoints.name: Get Project Context
endpoints.description: Return the org's conventions plus recent memories — what an agent loads at session start.

endpoints.name: Memory Graph
endpoints.description: Return memories and their links as a graph, for visualising how decisions relate.

keyFeatures.title: Multi-tenant by construction
keyFeatures.description: The auth middleware resolves an API key to a (user, org) pair and injects that scope into every downstream query. Cross-tenant reads are impossible by construction rather than forbidden by convention.

keyFeatures.title: An audit trail on every operation
keyFeatures.description: Every store, search and delete is recorded with user, tool and timestamp. This is what makes a shared AI memory acceptable to a team: an admin can always answer where a convention came from.

keyFeatures.title: MCP as the front door
keyFeatures.description: Agents connect over the Model Context Protocol, so Claude Code, Cursor and any other MCP client work without a bespoke integration each.

keyFeatures.title: One binary and one file
keyFeatures.description: Rust with SQLite bundled in. The whole deployment is `docker compose up` — no external database to provision, back up or operate.
